predictions.selection_reason: observable input from user configuration -> vm.runInNewContext execution -> arbitrary code execution vulnerability
predictions.source_summary: The value passed to vm.runInNewContext comes from user configuration through the ExecutionInterpreter. The regex pattern /#\{([^\}]+)\}/ extracts content between #{ and } which becomes m[1]. This content originates from configObj values that are processed during parsing.
predictions.sink_summary: The extracted expression m[1] is executed using vm.runInNewContext with an empty context object {}. This represents a direct execution of user-provided JavaScript code in a new context.
predictions.guard_summary: There are no validation, sanitization, or authorization controls on the content being executed. The code directly passes user input to vm.runInNewContext without any filtering or escaping.
predictions.risk_pattern: User-controllable JavaScript code is executed in a new VM context, allowing for arbitrary code execution attacks through configuration values.
predictions.context_summary: The vulnerability occurs in the ExecutionInterpreter.replace function where user-provided configuration values containing #{...} expressions are parsed and executed. The parsing process uses a regex to extract content between #{ and } which is then passed directly to vm.runInNewContext without any sanitization or validation.

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: Execution of user-controllable JavaScript code via vm.runInNewContext
